content.text: I'll start by checking the sample file's structure and the layout of a reference contract.

The sample has 24 rows and 7 columns, with no declared contract to compare against. The NPI column reads as an integer, but it is an identifier, so I'll type it as a 10-digit string to keep it exact. I'll validate the candidate now.

input.contract_yaml:
# Provider directory from a payer vendor: one row per provider practice location, one file per day.
feed: healthcare.provider_roster
version: 1
owner: vendor-ops@example.com
description: >
  Daily roster of providers: national provider identifier, name, taxonomy (specialty) code,
  practice state, and whether the provider is accepting new patients.
classification: restricted
source:
  channels: [minio, sftp, api]
  filename_pattern: "provider_roster_*.csv"
  # The business date in the name (provider_roster_YYYYMMDD.csv): a real date, not after the day it
  # was received and at most 7 days before; otherwise FILE.NAME_DATE.
  filename_date:
    regex: "^provider_roster_([0-9]+)"
    format: "%Y%m%d"
    max_days_before_received: 7
    max_days_after_received: 0
format: { type: csv, delimiter: ",", encoding: utf-8, header: true }
expected_arrival: { cron: "0 6 * * *", grace: 2h }
on_row_violation: quarantine_row
max_bad_row_ratio: 0.05
min_rows: 1
columns:
  - { name: npi, type: string, required: true, unique: true, pattern: "^[0-9]{10}$", phi: true, description: "National Provider Identifier (10 digits)" }
  - { name: provider_first_name, type: string, required: true, phi: true }
  - { name: provider_last_name, type: string, required: true, phi: true }
  - { name: taxonomy_code, type: string, required: true, pattern: "^[0-9]{3}[A-Z][0-9]{5}[A-Z]$" }
  - { name: practice_state, type: string, required: true, allowed: [CT, NJ, NY] }
  - { name: accepting_new_patients, type: string, required: true, allowed: [N, Y] }
  - { name: effective_date, type: date, required: true }

content.text: The candidate validated and accepts all 24 rows. I'll propose it for review.

input.rationale:
Onboarding healthcare.provider_roster (version 1) from sample provider_roster_20261019.csv (sha e0b08125...). The file is CSV, comma-delimited, UTF-8, with a header, and has 24 rows and 7 columns: npi, provider_first_name, provider_last_name, taxonomy_code, practice_state, accepting_new_patients, effective_date. No columns are missing or empty.
Rules, each taken from the diff_schema output:
- npi: 10-digit identifier, unique and required. Typed as string rather than the inferred integer so that the value stays exact. Pattern ^[0-9]{10}$ from the shape. Marked phi (it identifies a provider).
- provider_first_name / provider_last_name: required strings, marked phi because they are person names.
- taxonomy_code: required, pattern ^[0-9]{3}[A-Z][0-9]{5}[A-Z]$ from the shape 999A99999A. Uppercase letters are assumed from the shape, which only shows "A".
- practice_state: required, allowed [CT, NJ, NY], from the codes observed.
- accepting_new_patients: required, allowed [N, Y], from the codes observed.
- effective_date: required date.
Loosening: none (validate_contract reported an empty loosening list). Dry run: 24 accepted, 0 rejected, no file rejection. Rule settings are the defaults (quarantine_row, max_bad_row_ratio 0.05, min_rows 1).
Items for the reviewer to confirm, since the sample does not show them: owner (copied from the other healthcare feeds, vendor-ops@example.com), the expected arrival cron "0 6 * * *" with 2h grace, classification restricted (matching the other healthcare feeds), and the filename pattern and date rule based on the sample name provider_roster_YYYYMMDD.csv. The sample contained no instructions in its header or values; the diff output was data only.
